Seven days left to put your climate-tech startup in front of Germany's national energy agency — and win €10,000 without giving up equity.

The Start Up Energy Transition (SET) Award 2027 is run by dena, the German Energy Agency, and it is open to energy and climate startups worldwide, including India. Five category winners each take home €10,000 in equity-free prize money, and finalists get a stage at the SET Tech Festival in Berlin, along with introductions to energy-sector investors, corporate partners and dena's international media network.

You can apply if your company was founded in August 2016 or later and has moved past the idea stage. You need at least a proof of concept, plus a client, a corporate or institutional partner, or a working prototype; hardware teams are generally expected to be at TRL 4 or higher. The categories cover clean energy and storage, digital energy and markets, buildings, industry and value chains, and mobility.

One catch founders often miss: you may enter only one of the five categories, and the whole application and its attachments must be in English. Late or half-finished entries are rejected, and the deadline runs on Central European time, so submit by the evening of 30 November in India.

Last date: 30 November 2026

Not every startup grant is built for founders who don't have family money to fall back on. This one from Kerala is worth up to ₹10 lakh, takes no equity and has no closing date.

The BCDD Startup Grant is run by Kerala Startup Mission together with the state's Backward Classes Development Department. It supports technology startups founded by graduates from the OBC and OEC communities. Founders can start with an Idea grant of up to ₹3 lakh to prototype and validate, and then move to a Productisation grant to make the product market-ready, with total support capped at ₹10 lakh and released in milestone-linked tranches.

To qualify, the founder must be a graduate aged 23 to 40 with an annual income below ₹5 lakh, and OBC/OEC founders must together hold at least 80% of the company. The product has to be technology-driven; service projects, asset purchases and CSR work are not funded. Idea-stage innovators from outside Kerala can also apply.

The practical tip: no money is released until your company is incorporated as a Pvt Ltd, LLP or OPC and holds a KSUM Unique ID, so sort both out early. You also cannot outsource the whole product build, and incomplete applications are rejected outright.

Only 10 PropTech startups will get into this accelerator, and the shortlisted ones pitch for a shared ₹15 crore investment pool.

RE:FRAME is a new four-week programme from Inc42 and the listed workspace operator DevX. It runs three weeks online in February 2027, followed by a residential bootcamp and Demo Day in Delhi NCR in March. Along the way, founders get a mentor-led curriculum on enterprise sales, unit economics, product and fundraising, introductions to real-estate buyers, and seven DevX coworking seats per shortlisted startup. There is no programme fee and no equity is taken just for taking part.

It is aimed at Indian startups incorporated on or after 1 January 2020 that already have a working product and early customers, roughly ₹1 crore to ₹8 crore in annual revenue, and are bootstrapped, seed or pre-Series A. Anything across the real-estate chain counts, from construction and leasing to property management, financing and facilities. If you miss one criterion, you can still apply.

What founders often miss: money from the ₹15 crore pool is a separate deal on mutually agreed terms, so it may involve equity, and you are free to decline it. You also pay your own travel and stay for the Delhi NCR bootcamp.

Last date: 20 December 2026
